extracted_by: hand, T-0313 — the Democrat read, April 1834
note: Vol. I No. 21. The 'List of Letters' this issue carries is the HENNEPIN one, not Chicago's — T-0313 was written expecting the month's two letter lists here and on 30 April, and both of those are Hennepin's quarterly return signed by S. Galaher Jr.; the Chicago list is in the issues of 1 and 16 April. The issue's substance is John H. Kinzie's warehouse opposite Fort Dearborn in its fuller printing, a cabinet and chair manufactory on South Water Street, the bakery still standing where it stood on 8 April, and an estate notice that uses an attorney's office as a public address.

claims.notes: THE WAREHOUSE OPPOSITE THE FORT, SECOND WITNESS — and this printing reads 'WARE HOUSE' in capitals and keeps 'Agent for the Troy & Erie Line', which the 16 April strip lost. Two printings of the same copy, dated 14 April 1834, both placing John H. Kinzie's warehouse opposite Fort Dearborn: the placement is documented twice inside ten days and needs no inference. Taken with 1834-04-16 c001 this is the one building in the April corpus that a reconstruction can site against a structure whose own position is independently fixed.

claims.notes: A CABINET AND CHAIR MANUFACTORY ON SOUTH WATER STREET, and the offset the reconstruction wants is half-lost. 'Three doors' survives; what it is three doors from does not — the strip reads 'ee doors _' and then '} house, wil on', so the anchor is a house whose name the column edge cut away. The placement is therefore recorded as street_only with the offset text kept verbatim, rather than as a relative placement anchored on a building this pass would have had to name for it. The advertisement is dated 4 March 1834 and runs again on 1834-04-30 (p3 c5), so the works is documented across two months. Furniture made IN the town rather than shipped to it is a fact about the town's trades, and it is aimed squarely at the emigrants: 'all who are emigrating to this section of the country, will do well to call'.

claims.notes: THE BAKERY IS STILL THERE A FORTNIGHT LATER, at the same place and in the same words — 'in this town, on South Water-street, a few doors north of Newbury & Dole's store'. The same advertisement ran on 1834-04-08 (claim c001 there). Two printings is what turns a storefront from a notice into a WINDOW: D. Graves's bakery is documented on South Water Street from 8 April 1834 at the latest, placed against a building the corpus can locate on its own. That the copy is unchanged also settles that the two are one business and not two openings.

claims.notes: THE HENNEPIN LIST AGAIN — RECORDED, AND NOT MINTED. Same return as 1834-04-16 c005, printed a week later and cut differently: this strip keeps 'Whee]ley Brown 3', 'Jas. Booth', 'Josiah Clark', 'Michael Plaster sen.' and 'William Rood' where the 16 April strip kept 'Nathan Owen', 'B. Smith', 'Alpha Stephens' and 'Jesse Sawyer'. Neither printing is whole and neither mints anybody, because Hennepin is in Putnam County and its post office's letters say nothing about who was in Chicago (T-0292's rule for the Du Page, Plainfield and Hennepin lists). It is recorded so a later pass can see this list was read rather than skipped — an absence somebody looked for is evidence, an absence nobody looked for is a hole.

entities.role: attorneys at whose office claims against the estate may be left

claims.notes: A DEATH, AN ESTATE, AND THE LAWYERS' OFFICE AS AN ADDRESS. Bernardus H. Laughton is dead by April 1834 and David Laughton has taken administration; the notice also appears in fragment on 1834-04-08 (p3 c2, 'cuedle Bernardus H. Laughton, de[ceased]'). The line that earns this a card is the last one: claims against the estate 'may be left at the office of Collins & Caton' — which is a public instruction to go to a NAMED STOREFRONT, the attorneys' office on South Water Street placed at 1834-04-01 c005 and at 1834-01-28 c007. An address given as a place to leave papers is a stronger sign that a building was actually there and actually findable than an advertisement is. B. H. Laughton also stands in the 1 April letter list (1834-04-01 c002) with a letter waiting for him, which is the corpus's own before-and-after.
